title: Azure Monitor Logs and Advanced KQL
description: Use Azure Monitor Logs and KQL to diagnose issues, create workbooks, and build alert queries.

data.text: Azure Monitor Logs is the data platform behind Log Analytics. It collects structured log data from Azure resources, the Azure Monitor agent, and the Application Insights SDK. All data is stored in tables, and you query it with KQL.

terms.definition: The storage and query boundary for Azure Monitor Logs.
A table you create to store log data from your own applications.
A reusable KQL query stored in the workspace or Azure Monitor.
An interactive report that combines KQL queries, text, and visualizations.

data.text: Advanced KQL patterns let you analyze trends, detect anomalies, and correlate data across tables. Functions like arg_max, makeseries, and iif make it possible to build rich insights.

data.title: Detect Anomalous Error Rates (KQL)
data.content: Find endpoints whose error rate spiked in the last 24 hours:
data.code:
let baseline = AppRequests
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| summarize AvgErrorRate = 100.0 * countif(Success == false) / count()
    by bin(TimeGenerated, 1h), Name;
let today = AppRequests
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| summarize ErrorRate = 100.0 * countif(Success == false) / count()
    by bin(TimeGenerated, 1h), Name;
today
| extend Baseline = baseline[Name]
| where ErrorRate > Baseline * 2

data.title: Create a Time-Series Chart (KQL)
data.code:
AppRequests
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| summarize Count = count() by bin(TimeGenerated, 5m), ResultCode
| render timechart

data.caption: KQL query pipeline
data.definition:
graph TB
    T[Table: AppRequests] --> W[where: filter]
    W --> S[summarize: aggregate]
    S --> R[render: visualize]
    R --> CHART[Time Series Chart]

data.title: Save and Share Queries
data.text: Save useful KQL queries to build a shared library for your team. You can pin query results to Azure dashboards for at-a-glance visibility.

data.title: Build a Custom Log Query Workbook
data.description: Create a workbook that shows error trends for your application.
steps: Create a KQL query that shows error count by hour for the last 7 days.
Add a second query that shows the top 5 failing endpoints.
Pin both queries to an Azure Dashboard.
data.expectedOutcome: A dashboard with two tiles showing error trends and top failing endpoints.
